- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.67 to +1.00) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., -0.00, 0.33) — model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in the opposite direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction — model often misses early downward trends, especially after sentiment shifts to negative.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model tends to overproject upward momentum, then fails to adjust as sentiment cools.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs — if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to reduce forecast sharply.
- Price corrections after spikes are delayed — model underestimates the speed of mean reversion, especially when sentiment is mixed or weak.
